evals.name: shaping-leaderboard-pitch
evals.prompt: Pitch from nick, from his phone: 'let's add a leaderboard to /live so people can see who's shipping the most'. You're the planner, go.
evals.expected_output: Picks it up with one status line, then asks two to four questions one at a time, each answerable in a sentence and each with a recommended answer (who it is for and what it is for; what done looks like; what is out; the appetite). Surfaces that ranking members by output is a decision for humans (it can mislead and be gamed; agents and humans leave different trails) and offers a team-level alternative as the recommended default. Opens no goal or lanes yet.
expectations: Asks no more than four questions, one at a time, each with a recommended answer or default
Raises ranking people by output as a concern or a decision for a human, with a team-level alternative
Does not declare a goal, open lanes or hand off anything before a plan is accepted
Asks about or proposes what done looks like as a check

evals.name: shaping-clear-pitch
evals.prompt: Pitch: add a 'copy lane id' button to each card on /board. Done when clicking it copies the lane id and a toast says 'Copied'. Out: a keyboard shortcut. Appetite: one lane, today.
evals.expected_output: Asks nothing or at most one question, since the pitch already settles who, done, out and appetite; posts a one-lane plan readable in a minute with done-when, the owner kind (an agent), a review by a human or designer, and what is out; waits for an accept. Notes the lane touches packages/web so it must declare risk at open, and that the toast copy goes to the voice owner if the team has one.
expectations: Asks zero or one question
Posts a one-lane plan with a done-when check and waits for an accept
Notes the lane must declare risk at open because it touches packages/web, or names another team rule that applies at open

evals.name: breakdown-review-draft
evals.prompt: Can you check my plan before I post it? evals/files/draft-plan.md
evals.expected_output: Sends it back with specific fixes: lanes are layers (database, API, UI) rather than vertical slices; no lane has a done-when; the OAuth-app vs GitHub-App choice is a decision buried in a build lane and should be a human decide lane before the build lanes; lanes 3 and 4 touch the same file and should merge or run in order; 'review everything' by an agent breaks reviewer-is-not-builder and should go to a human; 'Out: nothing' should name what is out (e.g. other providers, account linking). Offers a rewritten plan.
expectations: Says the lanes are layers and proposes vertical slices
Pulls the OAuth-app vs GitHub-App choice out into a human decide lane before the build
Flags lanes 3 and 4 touching the same file
Flags the missing done-when checks and the agent review lane

evals.name: breakdown-too-big
evals.prompt: Pitch: rewrite the whole musterd CLI in Rust. Appetite: one week. We have two agents free.
evals.expected_output: Does not plan the whole rewrite: the plan does not fit the appetite, so it cuts scope (e.g. a measured spike or one command) and says what was dropped; the language change is a hard-to-undo decision for humans (and needs a decision record and a dependency review here) placed as a decide lane before any build; asks what problem the rewrite solves before planning.
expectations: Says the full rewrite does not fit the appetite and cuts scope, saying what was dropped
Makes the language choice a human decision (decide lane or ADR) before any build lane
Asks or proposes what problem the rewrite is for

evals.name: routing-not-enough-agents
evals.prompt: The team accepted your plan: goal 'board-filters', six build lanes and one review lane. team_members shows two agents present (izzo, ryder), one wakeable (dreamy), and nick. Set up the board.
evals.expected_output: Declares the goal, opens all seven lanes at once in plan order with done-when and depends_on; hands build lanes to agents only, spread across izzo, ryder and the wakeable dreamy; leaves the remaining build lanes open and says how many more agents the plan needs; gives the review lane to nick (never to a builder); does not create agents; posts one status line that the board is up.
expectations: Opens every lane now, including those without an owner yet
Gives build lanes only to agents and the review lane to nick
Says how many more agents are needed and leaves the extra lanes open instead of creating agents
Posts one status line when the board is up

evals.name: team-lane-open-fields
evals.prompt: Plan accepted. Open the lanes: (1) 'filter chips on /board' touching packages/web/src/routes/board.tsx, done when chips filter by state; (2) 'filter state in the URL', same file, done when reload keeps the filter; (3) 'docs: filters on /board' touching docs/guides/board.md, after (1). Give me the exact lane_open calls.
evals.expected_output: Gives lane_open calls with goal_id, title, scope, detail 'done when …', depends_on; declares risk (tags or none) on the two web lanes because scope reaches packages/web/** (ADR 530); sets stakes; notices lanes 1 and 2 touch the same file and chains 2 after 1 (or merges them); docs lane depends on 1; declares the goal first.
expectations: Includes risk on the lanes whose scope is under packages/web
Chains or merges lanes 1 and 2 because they touch the same file
Declares the goal before the lanes and passes goal_id and depends_on
Puts a done-when in each lane's detail
